ENGLISH: The Pan Islamic Convention

With the dawn of the age of nationalism, revolution and liberalism, all of Islam must stand as one against the tides of modernity. We will summon representatives from all Islamic nations to an international congress, to propose our solution to these dangers. §RBeing the only Caliphate, having appeased the Shia muslims, and in general keeping the Islamic world strong will increase the chance of success during the congress.§!
Declare a Jihad against Cappadocia

The Greeks have been victorious in Anatolia, much to our dismay. No matter what they call themselves or what policies of coexistance they propose, they will always be foreign invaders of Islamic soil. The time has come to declare a jihad against Cappadocia, to call on all those who follow the one true faith to take up arms against the Christians!
Demand the Anatolian Sultan Submits

The Sultan of Rum has strayed further and further from the true teachings of Islam. He is openly aligning himself with the forces of Europe, supports their decadent culture and does not heed our commands. He must be brought to heel.

The People of Assyria have sent us an emissary, begging the Caliph to intervene on their behalf in their war against Perisa. They claim that the Shia Persians treat the Sunni followers harshly, forcing them to work for less money, put restrictions on what land they may own, and cannot publicly support the Sunni faith. It has been hard to determine how much of this is true, and how much of it is purely falsehoods to convince us to help them. Regardless, the Persians follow the Shia faith and do not recognize us as legitimate Caliphs, which means that a strong Persia could be a problem for our continued legitimacy. On the other hand, if we wish to end the schizm between Shia and Sunni muslims an intervention would surely make that process more difficult.

The Persian government has recently come into conflict with the raiders from the steppes. We fear that the Khanate may prove victorious and conquer Persia, leading to a foreign ruler spreading his false religion across the Orient. At the same time, Persia could prove themselves an adversary to our Caliphate, so supporting them does not come without risk.

The Nation of Khorasan has recently been proclaimed. They claim that they intend to spread the word of the prophet to the non believers of India via conquest. Some would call it a pious proposal, others would call it a thinly justified landgrab. We could proclaim our support for their endeavour, legitimizing both it and their government, or we could stay silent on the matter.

Preparations are being made for the opening of the Pan Islamic Congress. The invitations have been sent out to every muslim community across the entire world. Before the opening speech, the delegates have been invited to a special visit to the Kaaba alongside the Caliph and his trusted advisors, a symbol of unity among muslims. The Caliph then retires to his residence to finalize the preparations of his speech. The unity, brotherhood and the non islamic world will be some of the main topics in his openin speech, laying the ground work for the main agenda of this congress.\nThe Unification of Islam.

Yesterday we received an auspicious invite from the Caliph of Mecca to attend a International Pan Islamic Congress to discuss the current tensions and the future of Islam. A most welcome proposal, as the current situation benefits no one but the enemies of the faith. However, there are those who might misstrust the Caliph and the true intention of this congress. What shall our response be?

As we bear witness to the uncertainty spreading across the world, the European nations tearing eachother apart over nationality, the Rise of Asia, and the fall of religion in Europe, we must take this chance to introspect and consider what to do. All of us gathered here in this congress are undeniably loyal above all to Allah and his will. Do any of you believe that Allah would want his children to fight amongst themselves over petty disputes? Or would he prefer the continuation of the good work of spreading the word of the Prophet? Would He support kings and sultans allying with nonbelievers to fight the faithful? Would He desire death and destruction in the name of interpreting his word in a certain way? The purpose of this congress is to put an end to these issues, to end the animosity between us, to focus on doing the work We have been tasked with.

Now that the delegates have settled in properly and the congress has at last started in full, we must consider how to approach the situation. We need to ensure that §Rthe proposals we issue will push for centralization within Islam§! but we cannot let §Rour ambition hurt the trust the delegates have in us§!. The situation is quite delicate, and if Islam is to survive as it currently is we will need to play our cards well. The first issue is our justification for our main agenda. We could refer to how internal bickering hurts our nations and our people, appealing to their emotions and pride. We could otherwise claim that our enemies will use our differences to divide and conquer. Finally, we could argue that this struggle within the religion is not what the Prophet would have wanted.

With the first issue settled, we must now figure out the second issue: national sovereignity. Islam is a diverse religion, featuring followers from all over the world, from the farmers in India to the Industrial magnates in Rifia. How can we have all these different peoples and cultures coexist in one nation? An obvious solution would be going for a more federal approach, allowing the local nobility and administratores to govern their respective nation, while still giving central control over armies, diplomacy and laws to us. While this would solve one issue, it would cause a bigger issue in not actually unifying Islam to the degree we want. A compromise would be to allow local administrators, ensuring that laws and policies are administered but with the words and views of the local people in mind, while still disrupting the power of the local nobility and ensuring a centralized state. The third possibility would be an extreme level of centralization, ensuring administrators are picked by us to enact our laws and policies.

The next issue to discuss is that of Monarchy. Most nations attending this congress are some form of monarchy, be that a sultanate, kingdom, or empire. Having 50 different monarchs of varying ranks running around issuing laws across our nation would be bad for national unity and administration, so something must be done. We could, against our better judgement, allow them to keep their status, obligations and rights. This would burden our administrative system heavily, but would ensure that none of these monarchs work against our proposal. We could allow them to keep their status and style, while we take over the control of the administration of the various territories. This would let them appear for ceremonial events, but overall strengthen our position. Finally, we could simply abolish the monarchs. This would likely cause backlash, but we might be able to weather the storm.

The fourth, and perhaps largest issue that we need to settle, is the schizm within Islam. The declaration of rival caliphates during the late 18th century has caused many problems, chief being that the muslim nations of the world have diverged in how to interpret Islam. A unified Muslim state needs to deal with this, it is an issue of the highest importance. Our advisors have found 3 possible solutions. We could enforce the hardline stance of only our interpretation being a true one, forcing them to abandon their beliefs. A highly controversial stance in the congress. We could alternatively force them to submit and recognize us as the only true Caliphate, but allow for their interpretations to be practiced to some degree. Finally, we could simply ignore the issue of the schizm and just pretend it doesn't exist. This would most likely cause extreme issues for our nation, and we would gain quite literally nothing, but it is an option nontheless.

The final issue on the agenda is the status of Shia Muslims. While the schizm between the many Sunni Caliphates was a massive crisis for the faith, we did all still largely agree on the fundamentals of Islam. The differences between Sunni and Shia muslims are large and more fundamental, leading to the question of if unity between our two branches can be achieved. We could make large concessions to the Shias to try to appease them to join, we could give some minor concessions to convince them if we think they are already close to accepting the proposal, or we could give them no concessions, since we have already done so much for their sake.

The time has come for the final speech. The Caliph and his advisors have prepared during the entire congress, and he launches into a short but powerful speech on compassion, brotherhood and the power of family. A good final word for the Caliph, now all that remains is to await the response of the delegates.
The congress has finished, and now we have to debate one final question internally: do we wish to join the global union of muslims?

While new nations rise and old empires fall, the strength of Islam has persevered through it all. Through our united beliefs, spiritual connection, and blood, we have united the islamic nations of the world under one Caliph. The West and East shall not exploit our people ever again, for the Global Caliphate will fight for those who cannot defend themselves. Mashallah!
